scenarios.title: One Nation governs alone
scenarios.detail: Needs 45 seats. Leading in 7. Short by 38.

scenarios.title: One Nation leads a right-wing government
scenarios.detail: One Nation would need more seats than the Coalition (60) and the two together to reach 45.

scenarios.title: One Nation is kingmaker for a Coalition government
scenarios.detail: Coalition leading in 60. If it falls short of 45 but Coalition + One Nation reaches it, One Nation can demand a deal. Coalition + One Nation = 67.

scenarios.title: Coalition governs alone
scenarios.detail: Coalition leading in 60. If it reaches 45 it doesn't need One Nation in the lower house.

paths.summary: On current leads the Coalition has a majority on its own, so One Nation's influence would come through the upper house rather than the lower house.

headline.title: Coalition on track to govern alone
headline.sub: One Nation projected to win 4 seats (likely range 2 to 6). Chance it decides who governs: 0%.

seats.name: Albert Park
seats.headline: One Nation out of contention
meaning: The VEC is counting preferences between Liberal and Labor, but Greens is ahead of Labor on first preferences. The real contest is likely Liberal against Greens, and the projection uses that.
One Nation is fourth on first preferences with 9.3%, behind Liberal on 37.2%.
The VEC's preference count is between Liberal and Labor, so it expects One Nation to miss the final two. If One Nation beats one of them on primaries, the VEC will redo the preference count.

seats.name: Bass
seats.watch: Contested outer seat; Roy Morgan expected a Liberal win
seats.headline: One Nation behind after preferences
meaning: One Nation is second on first preferences with 31.2%, behind Liberal on 34.7%.
To win, One Nation needs about 55.2% of the 34.1% of votes that went to other candidates to flow its way ahead of Liberal.
After preferences One Nation trails Liberal 43.6% to 56.4%.
Preferences from other candidates are flowing about 21.3% to One Nation.
Only 45.2% of counted votes have a preference count yet, so this can move.
Projecting that flow across every vote counted so far points to a loss (about 38.5% to One Nation after preferences).
The Labor candidate is third on 14.6%. Labor voters tend to put One Nation last, which hurts it here.
